name: Houses of the Divine
description: Stone circles, temples, cathedrals, mosques and shrines: how people have built to meet the sacred, from the Stone Age to Gaudi.

checkpoints.name: Stones, sun and pharaohs
checkpoints.note: The earliest monuments line up with the sun and the dead. Hunter-gatherers raised pillars at Gobekli Tepe, farmers built Newgrange, and Egyptian kings carved temples and pyramids on a vast scale.

checkpoints.name: Gods of Greece and Rome
checkpoints.note: Greek and Roman builders made temples for many gods, then Christianity gave their buildings and their ideas a second life. The Pantheon and the church of the Holy Sepulchre mark the turn.

checkpoints.name: Domes and early mosques
checkpoints.note: The domed Hagia Sophia showed what Byzantine builders could do, and soon the Dome of the Rock and the Great Mosque of Cordoba set the form of Islamic architecture. In Java, Borobudur became a Buddhist mountain.

checkpoints.name: The age of cathedrals
checkpoints.note: Gothic builders raised pointed arches, flying buttresses and wide windows at Chartres and Paris. Elsewhere Khmer kings built Angkor Wat and Ethiopian masons cut churches down into the rock at Lalibela.

checkpoints.name: Baroque to the modern
checkpoints.note: St. Peter's crowned Rome, the Golden Temple gave Sikhs a central shrine, and Djenne's mud mosque showed a Sahelian tradition. Cologne took six centuries and Sagrada Familia is still going.
